title: Tests repo: plant-products lifecycle coverage via API seed — draft resume, view, amend, cancel-amend, copy, delete
recipe: No recipe. The script is SIBLING-SET-PLAN.md §10.5 (the Features row's `notification-lifecycle` entry and the API/persistence row), §6.2 (the records-port → REST table: the four `PUT …/{ref}/status` transitions and `POST …/{ref}/copies` with an Idempotency-Key), FD-18 (what `/` does now, and why a bare `'/'` redirect would cross set boundaries) and R4 (copy idempotency mirrors live-animals on both sides).

filesToTouch.what: STEP 1. `git -C ~/git/defra/trade-imports-animals/repos/trade-imports-animals-tests branch --show-current` must print `spike/trace-to-requirements`. If not, STOP.

NEW. The plant analogue of `flows/live-animals/notification-actions.ts`. Drives the dashboard row actions and the action pages: `view(ref)`, `amend(ref)`, `cancelAmend(ref)`, `copy(ref)`, `delete(ref)`, plus the confirm/cancel steps each of them lands on.

Every method returns to a KNOWN place and the caller asserts where — do not bake the post-action assertion into the flow, because 'where does it land' is the R7 boundary this increment exists to pin.

NEW. The state machine, end to end against the real backend, seeded through `flows/plant-products/api-journey.ts` (pp-061) so no case re-walks 12 spokes.

CASES, each asserting BOTH the rendered state and `plantProductsApi.load(ref)`:
1. DRAFT resume — an API-seeded draft opens at `/plant-products/notifications/{ref}`, the hub shows the seeded rows' statuses, and continuing from a spoke saves onto the same document.
2. SUBMIT — a complete seeded draft submits; `status: 'SUBMITTED'` (`PUT …/{ref}/status`, §6.2 `finalise`).
3. AMEND — a submitted notification enters amend; `status: 'AMEND'`; edits are visible in the working document.
4. CANCEL-AMEND — discards the edits and returns to `status: 'SUBMITTED'` with the SUBMITTED BASELINE restored (§6.2: `{ status: 'SUBMITTED', discardChanges: true }`, D-4). Assert the edit is GONE, not merely that the status flipped — a status-only assertion passes on a cancel that forgot to restore.
5. VIEW — the read-only view of a submitted notification renders its values and offers no edit affordance.

Mirrors `tests/e2e/features/live-animals/promoted-lifecycle.spec.ts` in intent; write it fresh against the plant document.

NEW. The UI half of cancel-amend — the confirm page, its copy, the No/Cancel path leaving the amend in progress, and the Yes path discarding.

THE R7 ASSERTION THAT MATTERS: after confirming, the redirect lands under `/plant-products`, front-anchored. The live-animals equivalent redirects to a literal `'/'` (`sets/live-animals/.../features/cancel-amend/controller.test.js:104`), and pp-045 changes the PLANT equivalents to `dashboardPath()`. A plant controller that kept a bare `'/'` would now hit the FD-18 302 and drop the user into the LIVE-ANIMALS dashboard — a silent cross-set leak that renders a perfectly normal-looking page. Assert `^/plant-products`, never just 'not an error'.

NEW. Delete from the dashboard row action and from the notification itself: the confirm page renders with the right reference; No returns to where you were; Yes soft-deletes (`PUT …/{ref}/status` `{ status: 'DELETED' }`, idempotent per §6.2) and the row disappears from the list.

ASSERT: (a) the post-delete redirect is `^/plant-products`, NOT `'/'` (see the cancel-amend note — same leak); (b) `plantProductsApi.load(ref)` still returns the document with `status: 'DELETED'` — it is a SOFT delete, and a spec that asserts a 404 would be asserting the wrong contract; (c) the deleted notification is absent from `list` (server-side filter); (d) deleting twice is idempotent and does not error.

The live-animals equivalents to mirror in intent: `delete-notification/controller.test.js:56,80,83` (`noHref: '/'`, two `redirect: '/'`) and `tests/e2e/features/live-animals/notification-delete.spec.ts`.

NEW — and the ONLY end-to-end proof of the copy idempotency contract (R4, §6.2 `copy` row).

CASES:
1. Copy a submitted notification → a NEW DRAFT with a NEW `GBN-PP-…` reference, DOCUMENTLESS (accompanying documents are deliberately not copied — D-19), content otherwise carried over.
2. IDEMPOTENCY: the Copy button carries a `randomUUID()` minted per RENDERED action in a hidden input named `idempotencyKey`, sent as the `Idempotency-Key` header. Submitting the SAME rendered form twice (double-click, or a re-POST of the captured form) yields ONE new draft, not two. This is the assertion the whole R4 sequencing exists for and it cannot be made anywhere else — the frontend's stub records the key, but only the real backend enforces it.
3. SCOPED TO THE SOURCE REFERENCE: the same idempotency key against a DIFFERENT source reference DOES create a new draft. A backend that dedupes on the key alone passes case 2 and fails here.
4. RE-RENDER MINTS A NEW KEY: reloading the page and copying again DOES create a second draft — otherwise the button is dead after one use.
5. THE R7 BOUNDARY: after copying, the redirect lands under `^/plant-products` and the new draft opens at `/plant-products/notifications/{newRef}`. Never `'/'`, never live-animals.

NOTE THE TRANSPOSITION (§6.2): live-animals implements idempotency on the FULFILMENT resource (`POST /fulfilments/{id}/copy`, `adapters/http/notification-api-client.ts:51-55`); plant-products puts `/copies` on the NOTIFICATION resource (`POST /plant-products/notifications/{ref}/copies`). Transpose the pattern, not the path.

Add `plantProductsNotificationActions`, constructed from `plantProductsPages` (mirroring the live-animals `notificationActions` fixture at `:33-35`). Keep it beside the live-animals one; do not collapse them.

Add whatever action-surface locators these specs need and pp-064 did not: the dashboard row's action menu (View / Amend / Copy / Delete), the delete-confirmation page, the cancel-amend confirmation page, and — importantly — the Copy form's HIDDEN `idempotencyKey` input, which `copy-as-new.spec.ts` must read and re-submit to prove case 2.

The Copy button's form action and post-copy redirect are PREFIX-BEARING LINKS (built from `pagePath` / `hubPath` / `dashboardPath`), not route shapes — pp-055 says the same thing on the frontend side. So the form's `action` attribute should read `/plant-products/notifications/…`; assert that attribute directly in the spec. A bare `/notifications/…` action would post into nothing (or, worse, into whatever the other set serves).

flowChanges.lifecycle: DRAFT → SUBMITTED → AMEND → SUBMITTED (cancel-amend, baseline restored); DELETED (soft); copy → new DRAFT with a new reference

acceptanceCriteria: Branch verified as `spike/trace-to-requirements` before the first edit.
`flows/plant-products/notification-actions.ts` drives view / amend / cancel-amend / copy / delete and does NOT bake in the post-action assertion.
Every lifecycle case is seeded through `flows/plant-products/api-journey.ts` — no spec re-walks the 12-spoke journey to reach a state.
All five states are covered with BOTH a rendered assertion and a `plantProductsApi.load(ref)` assertion: draft resume, submit, amend, cancel-amend, view.
Cancel-amend asserts the EDIT IS GONE (submitted baseline restored), not merely that the status flipped back.
Delete asserts a SOFT delete: the document still loads with `status: 'DELETED'`, is absent from `list`, and a second delete is idempotent.

THE R7 BOUNDARY BAR: every post-action redirect in every one of these specs is asserted FRONT-ANCHORED on `^/plant-products`. No spec accepts a bare `/` — which would now 302 into live-animals via FD-18 and render a perfectly normal-looking wrong page.

THE IDEMPOTENCY BAR: re-submitting the SAME rendered Copy form yields ONE draft; the same key against a DIFFERENT source reference yields a NEW draft; a re-rendered form mints a fresh key and copies again successfully. All three, or the contract is not pinned.
The copied draft is documentless (D-19) and carries a new `GBN-PP-…` reference.
The Copy form's `action` attribute is asserted to be prefix-bearing (`/plant-products/notifications/…`).
npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm run format:check green.
Green against a co-resident stack; the live-animals suite unchanged in the same run.
notes:
THE TESTS REPO IS A SEPARATE GIT REPO — own remote, own branch (`spike/trace-to-requirements`), own CI, own package.json. Verbatim scripts: "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"; "lint": "eslint ."; "format:check": "prettier --check '**/*.{ts,js,mjs,md,json,yml,yaml}'"; "test": "npm run _assert_stack && npm run _clean && npm run database:reseed && npm run _test_e2e"; "test:local": "npm run test:integration"; plus `test:plant-products` from pp-060. Do not assume the frontend's scripts.

WHY THE R7 BOUNDARY ASSERTIONS ARE THE HEART OF THIS INCREMENT. Live-animals redirects to a literal `'/'` after delete, cancel-amend and copy — verified in the frontend at `delete-notification/controller.test.js:56,80,83`, `cancel-amend/controller.test.js:104`, `notification-actions/controller.test.js:132` and `dashboard/controller.test.js:403`. pp-045 changes the PLANT equivalents to `dashboardPath()`. If any plant controller keeps a bare `'/'`, FD-18's server-wide 302 forwards the user to `/live-animals` and they land in a fully-rendered, entirely wrong set's dashboard. Nothing errors. No log line. The only thing that catches it is a front-anchored URL assertion on every post-action redirect — which is why every one of these specs carries one, and why 'the page loaded' is never an acceptable assertion here.

WHY API-SEEDED, NOT UI-WALKED: reaching AMEND through the UI means completing 12 spokes and submitting, per case. `flows/plant-products/api-journey.ts` (pp-061) exists so lifecycle coverage costs seconds rather than minutes and so a lifecycle failure is attributable to the lifecycle, not to some unrelated page's validation.

COPY IDEMPOTENCY IS ONLY PROVABLE HERE. The engine port already carries the key (`engine/journey.js:125` `copyJourney(request, h, journeyId, idempotencyKey)`), the frontend mints a `randomUUID()` per rendered action into a hidden `idempotencyKey` input, and the set's `records/real.js` sends it as the `Idempotency-Key` header. The frontend's stub mirrors it with a dedupe key — but a stub proves the frontend sends the key, not that the SERVICE honours it. Only a real POST to `POST /plant-products/notifications/{ref}/copies` does. The three-case bar (same form twice = one draft; same key + different source = new draft; re-render = new key = new draft) is what distinguishes a real idempotency implementation from a backend that dedupes on the key alone or a frontend that reuses one key forever.

SOFT DELETE, NOT HARD. §6.2: `softDelete` is `PUT …/{ref}/status` `{ status: 'DELETED' }` and is idempotent; `list` hides DELETED server-side. A spec that asserts a 404 after delete is asserting a contract the service does not have and will fail for the right-looking wrong reason.

DEPENDS ON pp-045 (the frontend draft-lifecycle build) and pp-055 (copy idempotency on the plant records port). Both must have landed — R4 sequences the idempotency work BEFORE the Copy button ships, and this is the increment that proves the sequencing worked.

ROLLBACK: `git stash push -u`, never `reset --hard` + `clean -fd`.

Whether amend on a plant notification is blocked while another amend is in progress. Planned resolution: assert whatever the service does and record it; do not encode an expectation the backend design has not stated (SCHEMA-DESIGN §1.2's `submittedBaseline` implies one baseline, hence one amend at a time, but that is an inference).
